scope: Read-only defensive coverage and pursuit audit from retained numeric observations.

facts: A passing-side avoidance path preceded the opponent lateral acceleration.
The coverage policy requested a lateral recovery sprint while avoidance was returning from its previous heading.
The physically moving body spent approximately150ms completing that bounded return before requested sprint was allowed.
The jump subsequently occurred; native airborne permission shortened before the scheduled dive despite rising physical motion.
historicalFloaterDB5.interpretation: The initial lateral deficit increases how much of the later catch approach passes over the opponent. The return interval is consistent with bounded turning; unlike the later stationary-restart defect, no unsafe stale-heading reset is justified here.
historicalFloaterDB5.rejectedFix: 15,540 wider schedule candidates did not establish an early connected contact that avoids the observed native-state loss with adequate separation.
limitations: Proximity does not prove why native airborne state changed. A successful near-body swat control retained native airborne state.
No production coverage threshold or native-state override was added from this incident.

currentBulletDB14.prethrowDefect: An approximately83ms zero-input physical stop was followed by a reversal. The old150ms idle reset had not cleared steering, so unchanged avoidance initially moved opposite the new coverage request.
currentBulletDB14.fixedBehavior: Only a same-body stationary restart after a previous zero-input physical stop discards the stale heading; ordinary collision checks still choose the actual movement.

tackle.interpretation: The target changed direction before the predicted first window. Later proximity did not produce an authoritative tackle; the record does not expose a server rejection reason.

limitations: Correcting a prethrow movement defect is not a counterfactual guarantee of interception.
The tackle miss is separate from the stationary-restart fix.
No reachable catch was omitted by the observed initial aerial dispatch logic.
